what_its_for: Nafarelin is used to treat endometriosis (a condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus), which can cause pelvic pain and painful periods. It is also used in children to treat central precocious puberty (early puberty that starts too soon in children). It works by reducing the amount of certain hormones in your body.
how_to_take: Nafarelin comes as a nasal spray. Blow your nose gently before using the spray. Tilt your head slightly forward, put the tip of the bottle into one nostril, and spray while breathing in gently through your nose. Do not blow your nose for at least 30 minutes after using the spray. If your doctor has asked you to use a nasal decongestant spray on the same day, wait at least 2 hours after using nafarelin before using the decongestant. Alternate nostrils as directed by your doctor unless you are told to use both nostrils.
dosing: For endometriosis in adults: The usual dose is one spray (200 micrograms) into one nostril in the morning and one spray into the other nostril in the evening (400 micrograms total per day). Some women may need two sprays in each nostril twice a day (800 micrograms per day). Treatment usually lasts up to 6 months. For central precocious puberty in children: The usual starting dose is two sprays into each nostril in the morning and two sprays into each nostril in the evening (1600 micrograms per day). Your doctor may adjust the dose based on your child's response. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not use two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses may cause your symptoms to return or your hormone levels to change, so try to use the spray at the same times each day.
storage: Store the nasal spray bottle upright at room temperature, away from heat and direct light. Keep it away from freezing temperatures. Keep the bottle away from children. Do not use the spray after the expiration date printed on the package. Each bottle contains a limited number of doses — your pharmacist can tell you how many sprays are in your bottle so you know when to get a refill.
what_to_avoid: Do not smoke or use tobacco products, as this can worsen bone loss that may occur during treatment. Avoid drinking too much alcohol for the same reason. Do not use another nasal spray right after nafarelin — wait at least 2 hours. Do not get pregnant while using this medication, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use a non-hormonal form of birth control (such as condoms or a diaphragm) while on this medication, since nafarelin is not a contraceptive and irregular periods may still occur. Avoid missing doses, as this can reduce how well the medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: shortness of breath, sudden chest pain, or leg pain or swelling (possible signs of a blood clot); severe headaches, vision changes, or vomiting; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; mood changes, depression, or thoughts of self-harm; vaginal bleeding that is not your expected period; pain, redness, or discharge from the nose; bone pain; or if your child's puberty symptoms (such as breast growth or pubic hair) do not stop or get worse after a few months of treatment.
when_it_works: For endometriosis, you may notice improvement in your pain and symptoms within a few weeks to months of starting treatment. Menstrual periods usually stop within 4 to 6 weeks. For children with early puberty, signs of puberty (such as breast development or growth of pubic hair) should slow down or stop within the first few months of treatment. Give the medication time to work, and do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use nafarelin if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause miscarriage or harm to the baby. Use non-hormonal birth control during treatment. Breastfeeding: It is not known if nafarelin passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medication. Children: Nafarelin is approved for use in children with central precocious puberty. After stopping the medication, puberty should resume normally. Older adults: Nafarelin is not typically used in older adults. Bone health: Long-term use of nafarelin can cause bone thinning (decreased bone density). Talk to your doctor about ways to protect your bone health, such as getting enough calcium and vitamin D.
